description:
Follow-up to the merged canonical-JOB foundation (issue #289 Step 1). The
blind-spot audit surfaced two user-facing gaps the cutover introduced:

(A) NO REACHABLE SMALL VERSION OF THE REAL JOB WORKLOAD. The old synthetic
    generator scaled down to SF 0.001 so CI, laptops, and metered-egress
    cloud accounts could run "joinorder". Public `joinorder` is now a hard
    `--scale 1`: a ~1.2 GB download and ~5 GB working set (74,190,187 rows
    across 21 tables), with no smaller option. The fallback offered
    (`joinorder_synthetic`) is *different data* -- uniformly random, so it
    does not exercise the optimizer the way correlated IMDb data does -- and
    is `surface: "internal"`. The `tests/fixtures/joinorder_canonical_tiny`
    fixture exists but is a test artifact, not user-selectable. So today there
    is no quick-iteration path for the *actual* JOB workload. For a
    benchmarking tool whose users include people on laptops and metered cloud
    egress, that is a real ergonomics regression and should be a deliberate,
    recorded decision -- not an accident of the cutover.

(B) PARTIAL-MODE COMPARABILITY FOOTGUN. The DataFrame registry registers all
    113 canonical JOB query IDs, but only 13 have real translations; the other
    100 raise `NotImplementedError` and are in the default DataFrame skip list
    (`get_dataframe_skip_queries`). Previously the synthetic benchmark *had*
    only 13 queries, so DataFrame mode was 100% parity; now the public
    benchmark advertises 113 and DataFrame mode covers ~11.5%. If a
    `benchbox run --benchmark joinorder --mode dataframe` result (13/113, 100
    skipped) lands in results / leaderboard / compare looking like a complete
    `joinorder` run, that is exactly the comparability hazard the explorer
    work has been fixing for other benchmarks (PRs #361, #363, #367, #370 --
    leaderboard scope filters, compare comparability warnings, unranked
    evidence). This TODO verifies whether that hazard is already mitigated for
    joinorder and, if not, fixes it.

Two phases plus a conditional third. Phase 1 (A) ends in a recorded design
decision (with a decision gate -- AskUserQuestion). Phase 2 (B) is a
verification spike. Phase 3 (B) is conditional on Phase 2 finding a gap. The
phases are independent of each other and can be done in either order.

Related TODOs: `track2-joinorder-dataframe-coverage` (the actual translation
of the 100 stubs -- distinct from this TODO's "mark partial runs" concern;
cross-reference it from Phase 3). `joinorder-scale-stress-decision-framework`
and `joinorder-replicated-imdb-scale-prototype` are the *up*-scale (10x
bigger JOB) line of work; Phase 1 here is the *down*-scale (CI/dev ergonomics)
counterpart -- note the relationship so the two scale decisions stay
consistent, but do not merge them. Independent of
`joinorder-canonical-data-assurance`, `joinorder-redistribution-license-adr`,
`joinorder-step1-housekeeping`.

work_units.notes:
Lay out the options and put the decision to the user (AskUserQuestion):
  (a) BUILD "JOB-LIGHT": a sampled-but-correlated subset selectable as a
      new small scale (e.g. `--scale 0.05`). Requires: a deterministic
      subset-build step (extend `_project/scripts/build_joinorder_data.py`),
      a `joinorder-imdb-2013-v1-light` archive + manifest entry, a
      `light_reference_cardinalities.json`, `scale_options` += that scale
      in `benchmark_registry.py`, `JoinOrderBenchmark` mapping the scale
      to the light archive, tests, and docs. Acceptance criteria for
      "correlated enough" as in the context section above.
  (b) PROMOTE THE TINY FIXTURE: expose `joinorder_canonical_tiny` as a
      user-selectable scale with documented "smoke only -- not a JOB
      measurement, not comparable" semantics (and make sure such a run is
      marked unranked/partial like Phase 2/3 below).
  (c) DOCUMENT "NO SMALL PATH": accept that canonical `joinorder` is
      `--scale 1` only and `joinorder_synthetic` is uncorrelated
      smoke-only; make `docs/benchmarks/join-order.md` say so explicitly
      and close. (Lowest effort; leaves the ergonomics regression.)
